title: BDVM's "exact league scoring" drops all six reception yardage-band rules; WR fundamentals understated 19.7% and TE 22.0% on real 2025 data
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'No positional multipliers anywhere: Superflex/TEP/IDP format effects flow from exact scoring'; scripts/bdvm_build_baseline.py: 'scores them under the league's exact Sleeper scoring settings'.
observed: The live league scoring block carries base rec=0.08 and six per-reception YARDAGE-BAND bonuses (rec_0_4 0.17, rec_5_9 0.42, rec_10_19 0.67, rec_20_29 0.92, rec_30_39 1.17, rec_40p 1.92). src/nfl_data/realized_points.py — the only scorer BDVM's baseline uses — references none of those six keys and emits no diagnostic for unread scoring rules. Because base rec is only 0.08, essentially the entire per-catch economy of this league is dropped. 52 of 85 non-zero scoring keys are not literally referenced (most are DEF/K, legitimately out of scope; the six reception bands are not).

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json;s=json.load(open('/tmp/w13-contract-full.json'))['sleeper']['scoringSettings'];src=open('src/nfl_data/realized_points.py').read();print({k:s[k] for k in ('rec','rec_0_4','rec_5_9','rec_10_19','rec_20_29','rec_30_39','rec_40p')});print([k for k in ('rec_0_4','rec_5_9','rec_10_19','rec_20_29','rec_30_39','rec_40p') if f'\"{k}\"' in src])"  # then see the artifact for the per-position measurement
reproduction.expected: Every non-zero scoring rule the league pays is either applied or explicitly reported as unmodelled.
reproduction.actual: Six reception-band rules are silently dropped; the omitted points are position-correlated (pass-catchers only), so the fundamental board is biased BY POSITION, not merely rescaled.

numericProof.formula: omitted_ppg = 0.600 * receptions / games ; understatement% = omitted_ppg / (scored_ppg + omitted_ppg)

userImpact: Every WR and TE on the /bdvm board, and their 'Fund gap' cell on /rankings and /draft, is understated by roughly a fifth relative to QB and RB. A user reads that as 'the market overprices pass-catchers' and sells them.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed and re-measured against real 2025 nflverse data under the live scoring block. Prior said WR ~15% / RB ~9% / QB 0%; measured WR 19.7% / RB 8.1% / QB 0.0% and additionally TE 22.0%, which the prior did not report.

whatWorks: The 141-key scoring block IS read, and QB scoring is exact (0.0% understatement measured).
rootCause: compute_weekly_points is a fixed key->column table with no band arithmetic and no unread-key accounting. nflverse weekly rows are game aggregates and carry no per-reception yardage, so the bands cannot be computed exactly from this feed — but the code neither approximates them nor declares them unmodelled.
requiredRepair: Either estimate band bonuses from a per-player air-yards/aDOT distribution, or (minimum) emit the set of non-zero scoring keys the scorer did not consume into the BDVM payload meta so the board's own coverage is visible.
dependencies: Shared with any other workstream auditing src/nfl_data/realized_points.py (ROS, playerctx).

title: BDVM roster strategy capitals and the double-positive trade scan exclude every draft pick, omitting 8-52% of rebuilder capital and flipping 2 of 12 direction labels
claimUnderTest: src/bdvm/roster.py module docstring: 'produces, per roster: strategy capitals ..., now/future ratio, quick starter FPG, positional surplus vs. replacement, value-weighted age, pick capital, and a contend/retool/rebuild direction.' CLAUDE.md: 'GET /api/bdvm/roster (strategy capitals + league-relative direction per roster)'.
observed: analyze_rosters builds `assets` exclusively from roster['playerIds'] (roster.py:154-155). roster['picks'] is consumed only by len() for `pickCount` (roster.py:199). `capitals`, `nowFutureRatio`, `valueWeightedAge` and every asset the trade scan can propose are therefore player-only. No 'pick capital' field exists anywhere in the payload. The /bdvm Rosters table renders pickCount next to capitals computed as if those picks were worth zero.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python /tmp/.../w13_roster.py <out>  # then: see artifact; the counterfactual re-prices each roster's pickDetails through src.bdvm.picks.pick_values_all_strategies (mid-tier slot when Sleeper reports slot=null) and re-runs src.bdvm.roster._directions_relative
reproduction.expected: Rebuilder capital for a roster holding 62 picks should include those picks; direction labels should be stable under a correct capital.
reproduction.actual: Jason (62 picks): rebuilder capital 59,693 reported vs 114,477 with picks — 47.9% omitted. jstuedle (18 picks): 52.2% omitted. Ed flips retool->contend, Roy flips retool->rebuild.

userImpact: A user reading the /bdvm Rosters tab sees a rebuild-heavy team labelled 'retool' or 'contend' and trades against a direction that is wrong; the trade scan can never propose a pick, so it cannot find the pick-for-player trades that are the core of dynasty.

priorFinding.note: Independently found by code trace before opening the prior index. Prior recorded the omission qualitatively; this adds the measured magnitude (8.2-52.2% of rebuilder capital, median 21.6%) and the direction-label flips under the production _directions_relative thresholds.

whatWorks: Picks ARE priced by the engine — d['picks'] carried 120 priced distributions in the same run. The values exist and are simply never joined to the roster.
rootCause: The roster join is keyed on playerId; picks are keyed by name/label and were never given a second join path.
requiredRepair: Map roster['pickDetails'] (season/round/slot) onto the payload's pick distributions and add them to `assets` (or a separate pickCapital block that feeds nowFutureRatio). tests/bdvm/test_roster.py currently pins the player-only capitals and would need updating with the fix.
dependencies: W13-F004 — 5th/6th-round tier picks are unpriced, so even a correct join would drop them.

title: BDVM signal layer saturates at 81.5% STRONG_SELL: calibration anchors only the board maximum while the signal thresholds are absolute point values
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: the /bdvm board exposes 'fundamental-vs-market gap + signals' and the /rankings Fund-gap column is 'tinted by BDVM signal', with a tooltip asserting positive gap means the market underprices the player.
observed: DynastyEngine.calibrate anchors each strategy so only the TOP asset reaches target_top_value (9800). Nothing reconciles the SHAPE of the two boards below the top. On a real run over the live contract the fundamental board's median balanced value is 511.6 against a market median of 1914.5, so 92.6% of the 676 market-anchored assets carry a negative gap. Because signal_thresholds are absolute (strong_sell_alpha = -900.0), 570 of 699 priced players (81.5%) read STRONG_SELL, versus 10 STRONG_BUY and 69 HOLD.

reproduction.expected: An actionable signal distribution — a buy/sell board where the sell call means something.

numericProof.formula: signal = f(alpha), alpha = gap x liquidity, gap = tradeValue.balanced - marketValue ; thresholds fixed at +/-400 and +/-900

userImpact: The Fund-gap column on /rankings and the signal pills on /bdvm tell the user to sell four players in five. A signal that fires on 81.5% of the board carries no information, and the tooltip's stated interpretation ('positive means the market underprices') implies a calibrated comparison that has not been performed.

priorFinding.note: Measured with a reconstructed-baseline (proxy) snapshot built from ONE season back (2023/2024 nflverse pulls are not cached in this container). Production's 3-season baseline plus real Clay/IDP-Show sources will shift the magnitude. The STRUCTURAL cause — top-anchor-only calibration against absolute thresholds — is snapshot-independent, and the /bdvm page's own copy warns that proxy fundamentals are backward-looking, which is exactly the regime that produces this.

whatWorks: The two boards do agree where calibration touches them: fundamental max 9800 vs market max 9999. Signals are correctly suppressed to NO_MARKET (23 rows) where no anchor exists.
rootCause: calibrate() solves an anchor from the single maximum DV; the distribution below the max is whatever the surplus/discount stack produces, and it decays far faster than crowd market values. Absolute alpha thresholds then convert a distributional mismatch into a universal sell call.
requiredRepair: Either calibrate on a rank-matched quantile map between the fundamental and market boards before differencing, or make signal_thresholds percentile-based within the board. Whichever is chosen, the /bdvm page should surface the board-level gap distribution so saturation is visible.
dependencies: W13-F001 — the reception-band omission pushes pass-catcher fundamentals down and contributes to the negative skew.

title: Tier-form rookie picks in rounds 5-6 cannot be priced: the regex covers 1st-4th only, and the 24 affected rows are labelled with the factually wrong reason "unparseable_pick_name"
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: the /draft 'Fundamental pick values (BDVM)' panel shows 'balanced-strategy pick EV / hit% / median / ceiling beside the market anchor'; unpriced assets are 'unpriced with a reason'.
observed: _PICK_TIER_RE hardcodes (?P<round>1st|2nd|3rd|4th) and _ROUND_WORD has only four entries, so every 'YYYY {Early|Mid|Late} {5th|6th}' row falls through to distribution=None with reason='unparseable_pick_name'. This is a 6-round rookie draft: 24 of 144 pick rows (all of rounds 5-6 across 2026-2029) are affected. The slot-form parser accepts rounds 1-9, so '2026 Pick 5.03' prices fine while '2026 Early 5th' does not — the same asset class, two answers. The outcome model itself is not the limit: pick_values_all_strategies extrapolates past the last table anchor and returns 123.2 (round-5 Early) and 60.0 (round-6 Early) balanced EV for exactly these slots.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.bdvm.service import _parse_pick_slot;from src.bdvm.picks import pick_values_all_strategies;from src.bdvm.params import load_param_set;P=load_param_set();print([(n,_parse_pick_slot(n,12)) for n in ['2026 Early 4th','2026 Early 5th','2026 Mid 6th','2026 Pick 5.03']]);print({r:round(pick_values_all_strategies((r-1)*12+3,P,years_out=0)['balanced']['ev'],1) for r in (4,5,6)})"

userImpact: A trade containing a future 5th or 6th is reported as 'Not priced by the fundamental board' on the /trade BDVM panel even though the model can price it, and the /draft fundamental-pick panel is missing a third of the draft. The stated reason misdirects a maintainer toward the pick NAME rather than the round coverage.

priorFinding.note: Not present in the 21 prior BDVM findings. Adjacent to PRIOR-A15-F18 (pick outcome tail) but a different mechanism: that one is the outcome table, this one is name parsing.

whatWorks: The failure is HONEST — the pick is emitted with distribution: null and a reason, it appears in trade-eval's `unresolved` list rather than being priced at zero, and the /trade panel renders 'Not priced by the fundamental board: 2027 Mid 5th'. Verified by direct call.
rootCause: _PICK_TIER_RE and _ROUND_WORD were written against a 4-round assumption; the slot-form regex was later widened to \d and the tier form was not.
requiredRepair: Extend _ROUND_WORD/_PICK_TIER_RE to at least the league's configured rookie-draft round count, and rename the fallback reason to distinguish 'name did not parse' from 'round outside the model's coverage'.
dependencies: Feeds W13-F002 — a pick-capital fix would still omit these 24.

title: data/bdvm/ does not exist in this container, so all four BDVM routes answer 200 with status=no_projection_snapshot and every UI surface degrades correctly rather than fabricating a value
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: the engine 'answers status: "ok" with 726 players priced and 222 honestly unpriced'; the /rankings Fund-gap column 'gates on status == "ok" so it self-suppresses without a snapshot'; the /draft panel has the 'same silent-vanish posture'.
observed: The absent path is exactly `/home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/data/bdvm/projections/` (data/bdvm/ has no entry under data/ at all). All three GET routes return HTTP 200 with status='no_projection_snapshot', players/picks/unpriced all empty, and a message naming the fix. Nothing fabricates a value. In a real browser with /api/* re-routed to :8000 per the protocol: /rankings rendered 965 players with headers ['#','TIER','PLAYER','POS','CONSENSUS','VALUE','SOURCES','CONFIDENCE','EDGE','SIGNAL'] and NO 'Fund gap' column; /draft rendered its RookieBoard with 14 headers and no 'Fund gap'; /bdvm rendered an explicit 'No projection snapshot yet' panel, not a generic error. The bdvm_engine flag is default True and the routes are live.

reproduction.command: SECRET=$(cat .../e2e_secret.txt); curl -s -c /tmp/c.txt -XPOST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/test/create-session -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET" >/dev/null; for r in values roster trades; do curl -s -b /tmp/c.txt -w ' <- HTTP %{http_code}\n' "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/bdvm/$r" | head -c 200; done; ls data/bdvm 2>&1
reproduction.expected: Either priced values or an honest empty payload; no fabricated numbers; UI columns absent.
reproduction.actual: HTTP 200 status=no_projection_snapshot on all three; `ls: cannot access 'data/bdvm'`; no Fund gap column on either page; /bdvm shows the explicit state.

userImpact: None. The user sees no BDVM numbers rather than wrong BDVM numbers.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed as a data absence. The prior graded it Critical against CLAUDE.md's '726 players priced' claim; the AUDIT_PROTOCOL pre-declares the missing data/bdvm/ as Blocked by data, so the severity here is the documentation drift, not the empty payload. The silent-vanish and explicit-state claims in CLAUDE.md both hold at DOM level.

whatWorks: Route validation is correct too: surplusMode=bogus -> 400 bad_request; leagueKey=nope -> 400 unknown_league; anonymous POST /api/bdvm/trade-eval -> 401. Verified by curl.
rootCause: data/ is gitignored and a clean checkout has no BDVM snapshot; the audit harness does not run scripts/refresh_bdvm_projections.py.
requiredRepair: None in code. CLAUDE.md's '726 players priced / 222 unpriced' should be marked as a production observation, not a property of a checkout.

title: Nothing has ever validated a BDVM number: params_v1.json self-declares as un-backtested priors, src/bdvm/backtest.py has no caller outside its own test, and no user-facing surface says so
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'content-hashed paramSetId (config/bdvm/params_v1.json — priors, not validated truth)'. The question asked is whether that is honest.
observed: It is honest, and stronger than stated. params_v1.json's header says 'EVERY number here is a STARTING PRIOR ... informed by published research but NOT backtested truth'; pick_outcomes_v1.json calls itself 'explicitly the most placeholder-ish table in the whole model'. src/bdvm/backtest.py (336 lines, calibration/Brier machinery) is imported by exactly one file in the repo — tests/bdvm/test_backtest.py. Grep across the whole tree finds no script, no route, no workflow and no timer that runs it; the only other mentions are a comment in scripts/validate_consensus_edge_board.py that says 'Nothing in the repo does this' and two audit-evidence scripts. So no BDVM output has ever been scored against realized outcomes. On the UI, /bdvm discloses the PROXY projection flag well (per-row 'proxy' badge plus explanatory copy) and prints paramSetId as meta, but nothing tells the user the parameter set itself is unvalidated.

reproduction.command: grep -rn 'bdvm.backtest\|from src.bdvm import backtest' --include=*.py . | grep -v '\.venv' ; grep -n '_comment' -A 8 config/bdvm/params_v1.json | head -12
reproduction.expected: At least one production/script caller if the model's accuracy is ever measured.
reproduction.actual: Only tests/bdvm/test_backtest.py imports it; scripts/validate_consensus_edge_board.py:267 states in a comment that nothing in the repo does this.

userImpact: A user sees a signed 'Fund gap' and a STRONG_SELL pill and reasonably assumes the fundamental number has been checked against something. It has not — and given W13-F003 that gap is systematically negative.

priorFinding.note: Independently reached by reachability grep before opening the prior index. Adds the UI half: the proxy flag IS disclosed, the un-backtested parameter set is not.

whatWorks: Versioning is genuinely good: paramSetId is a content hash of the canonical JSON, so any edit produces a new id and every stored value is traceable. The engine reproduces the frozen reference exactly (see W13-F007). The disclosure that exists (proxy badges) is clear and honest.
rootCause: backtest.py was written as Phase-N scaffolding and never wired to a script or timer.
requiredRepair: Give backtest.py a CLI entry point and a scheduled run against realized seasons, and put the paramSetId's validation state (label 'bdvm-v1-priors') in front of the user next to the signal column.
dependencies: W13-F003 — a backtest is what would have caught the saturation.

title: The reference-parity test genuinely pins the Appendix-C numbers and passes: 13 archetypes x 3 currencies at +/-1.0, replacement levels to 2dp, startable slots exact
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'the production engine must keep reproducing its Appendix-C numbers (tests/bdvm/test_engine_parity.py)'.
observed: The golden values in test_engine_parity.py are not regenerated self-consistency numbers — every one of the 13 x 3 trade values, the 7 replacement FPGs and the 7 startable-slot counts matches docs/research/bdvm-v1/reference/examples_output.txt token for token (e.g. p1 (9800, 7974, 6265); QB replacement 12.40; LB startable 48). test_reference_parity.py separately re-executes the frozen run_examples.py and diffs its stdout against the committed golden output token-for-token, and asserts no production module imports the reference. The full BDVM suite is 284 tests, all passing on Python 3.11.15 (CI uses 3.12).

reproduction.expected: all pass, with parity actually comparing against the frozen fixture

userImpact: None — this is a positive result.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covered parity quality.

requiredRepair: Minor: only 4 of the 13 probability rows are pinned in the production parity test (p3, p4, p9, p12), and the value-decomposition / pick / CES-trade / roster-report blocks of the reference are guarded only by the reference-side token diff, not by a production-side assertion. Widening the production parity to all 13 probability rows would be cheap.

title: Market isolation is structurally real: nothing in src/bdvm/ reads a market value before the market layer, and only value-signal sources are ever read as prices
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'Fundamentals compute with ZERO market inputs; the market layer (src/bdvm/market.py) runs strictly afterward and reads only value-signal sources (ktcSfTep/ktc/idpTradeCalc — never the rank-signal synthetic encodings in canonicalSiteValues)'. Also: 'It never touches rankDerivedValue'.
observed: Verified four ways. (1) Grep for rankDerivedValue / _finalAdjusted / canonicalSiteValues / ktc / idpTradeCalc / marketValue across src/bdvm/*.py returns hits ONLY in market.py, plus three post-hoc reads of the already-computed `market` block in roster.py:168/228-229 and service.py:641 — no pre-fundamental read anywhere. (2) engine.py imports only curves, league_config, params, pool, replacement, surplus, survival, uncertainty — no market module. (3) market.py raises MarketIsolationError (market.py:218) when asked to run before fundamentals exist, and tests/bdvm/test_market_isolation.py has 15 tests including test_market_before_fundamentals_raises and test_market_never_mutates_fundamentals. (4) The three sources market.py will read (ktcSfTep, ktc, idpTradeCalc) are all genuine value-signal boards: data_contract.py documents that standard `ktc` was retired from the BLEND on 2026-04-28 but its native values are still loaded into canonicalSiteValues, so the ktc fallback is not the 999900-rank*100 synthetic encoding. On the live run, market anchors resolved as ktcSfTep 368, idpTradeCalc 308, none 23 — exactly the offense/picks-vs-IDP split market.py documents.

reproduction.expected: no pre-fundamental market read; isolation tests pass
reproduction.actual: only post-fundamental reads in roster.py/service.py and a docstring mention in __init__.py; 15 isolation tests pass

priorFinding.note: No prior finding disputed isolation; verifying it was in scope and it holds.

requiredRepair: One cosmetic gap: meta.marketReadAfterFundamental is a hardcoded `True` literal (src/bdvm/service.py:297), not a computed assertion. A payload field that asserts a safety property but can never be False is decoration; the real guarantee is the MarketIsolationError raise and the import graph. Either compute it or drop it.

title: The aging/survival split is real and correctly wired: conditional productivity uses mileage-adjusted effective age, hazard uses chronological age, at the call site
claimUnderTest: curves.py: 'Conditional production ONLY ... Loss of role / disappearance belongs to survival.py; merging the two is the #1 double-counting failure in public dynasty models'. survival.py: 'Hazard uses CHRONOLOGICAL age; mileage-adjusted effective age belongs to the aging curve only'.
observed: Two genuinely separate curves doing two genuinely separate jobs, and the separation survives at the call site — which is where this normally breaks. In DynastyEngine.season_path: line 197 computes a_eff = effective_age(pos, age_t, career_load + t*load_rate) and line 198 feeds ONLY that to aging_mult; line 238 calls hazard(params, pos, age_t, ...) with the raw chronological age_t. The payload confirms it per row: A.J. Brown t=5 shows age 34.0 alongside age_eff 34.22, and the survival column moves on the chronological ladder. Expected value per season is the product ssv(t) x S(t) (engine.py:256), so the two enter multiplicatively rather than one curve absorbing both. survival.py additionally exposes expected_remaining_seasons = sum S(t), which is only meaningful because S is a pure survival function.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W13/engine-live-run.json'));p=[x for x in d['players'] if x['name']=='A.J. Brown'][0];print([(r['t'],r['age'],round(r['age_eff'],2),round(r['survival'],3)) for r in p['path']])"
reproduction.expected: age_eff >= age and diverging with career load; survival indexed on chronological age

numericProof.formula: E[value_t] = E[max(0, X_t - R)] * G * prod_{k<=t}(1 - h(k))

priorFinding.note: No prior finding disputed the split.

title: Expected-positive-surplus E[max(0, X-R)] is genuinely implemented (not max(0, E[X]-R)) and the three-mode ablation is live — but it pays 404 of 424 below-replacement players
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'surplusMode=option|truncated|plain exposes the option-value ablation'. surplus.py: 'SSV(t) = E[max(0, X - R)]G = [(µ-R)Φ(z) + σφ(z)]G ... This is the central V1 HYPOTHESIS, not a law.'
observed: The closed form is exactly right and it is what runs. I recomputed expected_positive_surplus(mu, sigma, R) * games independently on all 4,893 path rows of a real 699-player run and matched the payload's ssv to 0.000e+00 max absolute error. p_above_replacement matched Phi(z0) to 0.000e+00. The ablation is real and reachable: /api/bdvm/values?surplusMode=bogus returns 400, and the three modes produce materially different boards (Aaron Rodgers balanced: option 429.4 / truncated 0.0 / plain 0.0). The quantile band shares the functional, so floor <= median <= ceiling held on 699/699 rows with zero violations. The methodological consequence is the one the prior audit flagged: because sigma > 0 always, E[max(0,X-R)] > 0 even when mu < R, so 404 of the 424 players projected BELOW replacement still carry positive balanced trade value.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.bdvm.surplus import expected_positive_surplus as f;d=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W13/engine-live-run.json'));e=max(abs(f(r['mu'],r['sigma'],r['R'])*r['games']-r['ssv']) for p in d['players'] for r in p['path']);print('max ssv err',e);b=[p for p in d['players'] if p['raw']['fpg']<p['raw']['replacement']];print(len(b),'below repl;',sum(1 for p in b if p['tradeValue']['balanced']>0),'still priced >0')"
reproduction.expected: ssv reproduces the option formula; below-replacement players priced at 0 under truncated/plain
reproduction.actual: max ssv err 0.0 ; 424 below replacement, 404 still priced > 0 under the default option mode

userImpact: A player the model projects below replacement still shows a four-figure fundamental value. That is defensible (you can bench him) but it is a hypothesis, and per W13-F006 it has never been tested against realized outcomes.

priorFinding.note: The prior graded this High as a defect ('assumes ex-post lineup selection and awards positive value to below-replacement projections'). Confirmed factually — 404/424 measured — but the label is wrong: it is a documented, flag-exposed hypothesis with a working ablation, not an unintended behaviour. Downgraded to a validation gap (W13-F006), not a math error. Separately REFUTES the implied concern that the simpler max(0, E[X]-R) was shipped by mistake: the option form is exact to 1e-9 and the other two are selectable.

whatWorks: The formula, the ablation endpoint, the 400 validation, and the band monotonicity fix (0 violations on 699 rows) all verified at runtime.
requiredRepair: Measure it. The ablation exists precisely so the champion can be dethroned; nothing runs it.

title: Prior finding refuted: range.ceiling_p85 no longer escapes the 0-10000 scale — max is exactly 9999 across 699 players, 0 rows over cap
claimUnderTest: PRIOR-A15-F10: 'range.ceiling_p85 escapes the advertised 0-10000 scale (up to 19,843) and is rendered without a cap'.
observed: Not reproducible. to_trade_value now applies a strictly increasing squash (not a min() clamp) at scale.trade_value_max, and every number on the 0-10000 display scale — per-strategy trade values AND the floor/median/ceiling band — leaves through it. On a real 699-player run the maximum ceiling_p85 is 9999 and zero rows exceed 10000. The engine's own comments cite the ~20k p85 measurement the prior described and explain why a hard clamp was rejected (it collapsed seven distinct ceilings onto one value, which frontend/lib/bdvm.js then renders as a tie).

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W13/engine-live-run.json'));c=[p['range']['ceiling_p85'] for p in d['players']];print('n',len(c),'max',max(c),'over 10000:',sum(1 for x in c if x>10000))"

numericProof.formula: squash at scale.trade_value_max applied inside to_trade_value

userImpact: None — the prior defect is fixed.

priorFinding.note: Measured on a proxy-baseline snapshot of the live contract. The fix is structural (the squash is inside to_trade_value, which every scale output passes through), so it does not depend on which snapshot is loaded.

whatWorks: The bound is order-preserving, which the naive fix would not have been.

title: Prior finding refuted: the rookie-pick outcome table no longer prices every deep pick identically — 38 distinct EVs across the 48 slots from 3.01 to 6.12
claimUnderTest: PRIOR-A15-F18: 'Rookie-pick outcome table has no rows past overall slot 36 — every pick from 3.01 down is priced identically'.
observed: Mostly not reproducible. _outcome_row now EXTRAPOLATES past the last tabulated anchor (slot 36) by continuing the last measured segment's per-slot geometric decay component-by-component, with the ratio clamped to (0,1] so a non-monotone table cannot make deep picks grow; the docstring cites this as the fix for 'audit M7'. Measured on the real board: the 48 slots from 2026 Pick 3.01 to 6.12 carry 38 distinct balanced EVs, decaying monotonically from 650.0 to 35.3. A narrower residual of the prior finding does survive: INSIDE the table, nearest-anchor snapping (anchors are 1,2,3,4,6,8,12,16,24,36) still collapses slots 25-30 onto anchor 24, so 2026 Pick 3.01 through 3.06 are all exactly 650.0.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W13/engine-live-run.json'));e={p['name']:round(p['distribution']['balanced']['ev'],1) for p in d['picks'] if p.get('distribution') and p['name'].startswith('2026 Pick')};s=[(k,v) for k,v in sorted(e.items()) if k>='2026 Pick 3.01'];print(len(s),'slots',len({v for _,v in s}),'distinct');print(s[:6],s[-4:])"
reproduction.expected: distinct, monotonically decaying EVs past slot 36

userImpact: Marginal — six consecutive third-round slots price identically, which slightly overvalues 3.01 relative to 3.06.

priorFinding.note: The headline claim ('every pick from 3.01 down is priced identically') is refuted — the extrapolation fix is in and works. The residual within-table nearest-anchor collision on slots 25-30 is real but an order of magnitude narrower than described.

whatWorks: The extrapolation, its monotonicity clamp, and the tail values.
rootCause: The anchor table has a 12-slot gap between 24 and 36 and nearest-neighbour resolution inside the table.
requiredRepair: Interpolate between anchors instead of snapping to the nearest one.
dependencies: W13-F004 — separately, 24 tier-form picks never reach this code at all.

title: Prior findings refuted: STRONG_BUY is reachable (10 players on a real board) and liquidity now DECREASES with market disagreement
claimUnderTest: PRIOR-A15-F02: 'STRONG_BUY is structurally unreachable in production — gap_persisted_days is never passed'. PRIOR-A15-F07: 'liquidity increases with market DISAGREEMENT and multiplies the gap into alpha — inverted semantics'.
observed: Both not reproducible. (F02) On a real 699-player board 10 players carry STRONG_BUY, and tests/bdvm/test_market_isolation.py has an explicit test_strong_buy_is_reachable_without_gap_history beside test_strong_buy_requires_persistence_and_liquidity — the persistence requirement now has a no-history path. (F07) The liquidity config now reads 'liquidity = clip(base - dispersion_coeff * dispersion, clip_lo, clip_hi)' with base 1.0 and dispersion_coeff 1.6, and its own comment states the sign was corrected: 'Dispersion SUBTRACTS: cross-source disagreement about the price makes an asset harder to transact'. Live rows confirm the direction: A.J. Brown marketDispersion 0.0225 -> liquidity 0.964 (near clip_hi). Separately, _dispersion_for_row was narrowed on 2026-08-04 to ONE field with an explicit note that it previously mixed marketDispersionCV, sourceRankPercentileSpread and a hardcoded 0.20, and unmeasured rows now take clip_lo so they are HARDER to signal on, not easier.

reproduction.expected: STRONG_BUY count > 0; liquidity high when dispersion low

userImpact: None — both prior defects are fixed.

priorFinding.note: Also refutes PRIOR-A15-F07 (liquidity sign). Note that STRONG_BUY being REACHABLE does not make the signal layer healthy — see W13-F003, where the same board reads STRONG_SELL on 81.5% of players.

title: Prior finding partially refuted: risk_neutral and balanced differ by 3.7% at the median (not 1-2%), but the four strategy currencies still collapse toward three
claimUnderTest: PRIOR-A15-F09: 'risk_lambda moves values by 1-2%: risk_neutral is a near-duplicate of balanced after anchoring, so the four strategy currencies are really three'.
observed: Partially reproducible with a corrected magnitude. Over the 566 players with balanced trade value above 100, |risk_neutral - balanced| / balanced has median 3.70%, p90 10.50% and max 19.07% — three to five times the prior's stated 1-2%, but still the smallest spread among the four currencies (contender/balanced/rebuilder differ by hundreds of percent: A.J. Brown 1830 / 1075 / 508). The mechanism is as described: risk_neutral shares balanced's discount and usability vector and differs only by risk_lambda=0.1 vs 0.0, and calibrate() re-anchors each currency independently to the same target_top_value, which removes most of the level difference the lambda created.
userImpact: The /bdvm strategy selector offers four currencies; two of them answer nearly the same question, which overstates how much analysis the selector performs.

priorFinding.note: Direction confirmed, magnitude refuted (3.70% median, not 1-2%). Measured on a proxy-baseline snapshot; a wider-sigma real projection set would widen the lambda term further.

whatWorks: contender / balanced / rebuilder are genuinely distinct currencies and the parity test pins all three against the reference.
rootCause: Per-currency re-anchoring to a common target_top_value absorbs most of the risk_lambda level effect.
requiredRepair: Either anchor risk_neutral on the balanced anchor (so the lambda difference survives calibration) or drop the fourth currency from the UI selector.

title: Every projection in a reconstructed-baseline snapshot reports sigmaSource 0.0, so projection-source disagreement contributes nothing to sigma
claimUnderTest: PRIOR-A15-F08: 'Seven parameter sections in params_v1.json are never read; the most consequential leaves single-source projections with sigma_source = 0'.
observed: Reproduced, with an important confound the prior did not state. On a real run every one of the 699 priced players carries projection.sigmaSource == 0.0 and sourceCount == 1. But that snapshot IS single-source by construction (reconstructed baseline only — no Clay, no IDP Show, because data/bdvm/ is absent and 2023/2024 nflverse pulls are not cached here), so a zero cross-source dispersion is the CORRECT answer for it, not a dropped parameter. What this run can establish is the consequence, not the cause: when only the proxy baseline is available, the entire sigma comes from the positional CV prior and none of it from projection disagreement, and nothing in the payload distinguishes 'sources agreed' from 'there was one source'. sourceCount is stamped, so the information is present but the sigma is not differentiated.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W13/engine-live-run.json'));z=[p for p in d['players'] if p['projection']['sigmaSource']==0.0];print(len(z),'/',len(d['players']),'sourceCounts',{p['projection']['sourceCount'] for p in z})"
reproduction.expected: sigma_source > 0 where multiple projection sources disagree
reproduction.actual: 699/699 at sigmaSource 0.0, all sourceCount 1 — the snapshot has one source, so this run cannot separate 'never read' from 'nothing to read'

userImpact: On a proxy-only board, confidence buckets and the floor/ceiling band understate how little is actually known, because the one uncertainty channel that would register 'we have a single backward-looking source' is inert.

priorFinding.note: Symptom reproduced exactly (699/699 at 0.0) but the cause cannot be isolated in this container because no multi-source snapshot can be built without network access to Clay's CDN PDF and The IDP Show's authenticated sheet. Unblocking requires either data/bdvm/projections/ from production or those two fetches, both outside this audit's network permissions.

whatWorks: sourceCount, sources, anyProxy, staleSources and vocabularyLimitedSources are all stamped per player, so the provenance IS visible even where sigma does not move.
rootCause: Undetermined here — either the parameter section is unread, or a single-source snapshot legitimately yields zero dispersion.
requiredRepair: Reproduce with a two-source snapshot before acting. If sigma_source stays 0.0 with sourceCount >= 2, the prior's diagnosis is confirmed.
dependencies: Blocked by the same missing data as W13-F005.

title: meta.marketReadAfterFundamental is a hardcoded True literal and the values cache is keyed partly on id(contract), a reusable CPython address
claimUnderTest: The payload advertises marketReadAfterFundamental as a property of the run. PRIOR-A15-F16: 'get_bdvm_values cache key contains id(contract), a reusable CPython address'.
observed: Two small honesty/robustness items in the same layer. (1) service.py:297 writes 'marketReadAfterFundamental': True as a literal into every meta block. It can never be False, so it asserts a safety property it does not check — the actual guarantee lives in market.py's MarketIsolationError and the import graph (W13-F008). (2) The values cache key is (id(contract), contract['generatedAt'], league_key, param_set_id, snapshot_path, surplus_mode, current_week, day, events_fingerprint). id() of a freed object can be reused — but generatedAt co-keys it, so a collision additionally requires an identical generatedAt, which in practice means the identical scrape. The risk is therefore much lower than the prior implies; the id() term is nonetheless doing no useful work that generatedAt is not already doing better.

reproduction.expected: a computed assertion, and a cache key made only of content identifiers
reproduction.actual: a `True` literal; an id() term in the key tuple

userImpact: None directly. A reader of the payload may take marketReadAfterFundamental as evidence rather than as a comment.

priorFinding.note: id(contract) confirmed present; severity downgraded because generatedAt co-keys the tuple, so an address collision alone cannot serve stale data. The marketReadAfterFundamental half is new.

whatWorks: The rest of the cache key is sound, and the events-file fingerprint genuinely invalidates on a news-ingest write.
requiredRepair: Drop the id() term; either compute marketReadAfterFundamental from the call order or remove it.
